summary: This diff is purely additive (5 new files + one YAML metadata edit closing out a phase-plan entry) inside claude-control/ai-os-scripts, with no changes to migrations, schema, auth, permissions, payments, billing, rls, security paths, .env files, or .github/workflows/**, so the tier1 classification is correct and consistent with the hard rules in SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md. The new scripts (document_engine.py, notification_engine.py, notify-owner.py) use subprocess.run with argument lists (never shell=True or string-interpolated shell commands), so there is no command-injection surface; API keys are read from an external env file rather than embedded in source; JSON parsing/encoding is used correctly throughout. The detect_duplicate_documents_by_hash port, the notify-owner.py dedupe/rate-limit logic, and the close_phase4 regex-anchored YAML surgery (verified against the actual before/after diff context) are all logically sound. The work honestly scopes itself to the claude-control repo boundary and documents, rather than fabricates, cross-repo integration it did not build, consistent with the precedent set by Phases 1-3.
issues: No automated tests accompany the new CLI scripts (document_engine.py, notification_engine.py, notify-owner.py); the diff's claimed 'real_evidence' command outputs (live Resend sends, capability registration counts, etc.) cannot be independently verified from the diff alone and should be spot-checked by a human/audit step before being relied on.

scripts/notify-owner.py hardcodes the Owner's personal email address and a resend.dev sandbox From-address directly in source now permanently committed to git history (previously only lived untracked at /opt/veridian/scripts/notify-owner.py) -- low risk given it's a single-owner internal alerting tool, but worth confirming this is acceptable to commit long-term.

The task title references unifying 'pdf-generator.ts' but no functional AI-OS-layer integration was built for PDF generation -- it is only cataloged in the capability registry with reachable_from_ai_os_layer: false, so this deliverable is largely schema/documentation rather than a functional unification for that specific operation; not a defect, but worth noting as a scope/title mismatch.
